Decision: split the write surface in two. Item-level writes (create, move, edit, note, triage, resume, dispatch, stop) stay available wherever the board is reachable — that is the collaborative surface and the reason --host exists. Administrative writes that change the rules of the board itself (stages, gates, config) are refused unless the request arrived on loopback, regardless of --host. Rationale: a colleague on the LAN moving a card is the feature; a stranger on hotel wifi deleting your stages, disabling a gate, or enabling the runner is not. The guard is cheap, needs no auth system, and keeps the property that gw serve never becomes a remote administration console.
